name: Shedd Aquarium
description: One of the world's largest indoor aquariums on the shores of Lake Michigan. Home to 32,000 animals including beluga whales, dolphins, sea otters, and penguins. The Caribbean Reef exhibit with its 90,000-gallon circular tank is a family favorite. Interactive touch pools and a 4D theater make it highly engaging for kids.
location: 1200 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
tipsAndTricks: Buy timed-entry tickets online at least 3 days ahead — weekend walk-ups regularly sell out by noon.
The 'Animal Spotlights' talks at 10:30am and 2pm are free with admission and offer close-up views you can't get otherwise.
Pack a layer — the polar play zone is kept at a chilly 46°F and toddlers feel it fast.
Free admission days (Illinois residents only, typically Wednesdays in January/February) are packed — avoid unless budget is tight.
The stroller parking near the main dolphin tank fills early — arrive before 9:45am or plan to babywear.

parentStory.title: Beluga whisperer for a day
parentStory.excerpt: Our 5-year-old has been obsessed with beluga whales since she saw a documentary. When the trainer brought Kayla the beluga right up to the glass during the morning talk, she pressed her tiny hand against the pane. Kayla mirrored her. They held hands through the glass for a full minute.
parentStory.author: Mike, dad of 1 from Indianapolis
parentStory.fullStory: We drove 3 hours just for the aquarium — our daughter's choice. She has been drawing belugas since she was 3. The morning trainer talk at the Abbott Oceanarium was incredible. The trainer signaled, and Kayla swam right over and pressed her melon against the glass. Without being told, our daughter pressed her palm up. They stayed that way for maybe 60 seconds. Every kid in the audience went quiet. I'm not ashamed to say I cried.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Caribbean Reef, Amazon Rising, Oceanarium show, touch pool — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All exhibits, 4D theater, Stingray Touch, behind-the-scenes tour, lunch at the aquarium — 5-6 hours

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
description: One of the last free-admission zoos in the United States, located in Chicago's beautiful Lincoln Park neighborhood. Home to over 1,100 animals including polar bears, gorillas, chimpanzees, and red pandas. The Farm-in-the-Zoo petting area is a hit with toddlers. The zoo is exceptionally well-maintained with wide, flat paths perfect for strollers.
bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon, May-October
tipsAndTricks: Park at the zoo's discounted North Lot (enter on Stockton) — nearby garages charge 3x more.
The Farm-in-the-Zoo opens at 10am but the barn doors open at 10:30 — arrive then to beat the school groups.
Bring swim diapers — the Pritzker Family Children Zoo water play area opens Memorial Day weekend and is irresistible.
Free admission doesn't mean free parking — book an Explore and More parking pass online for 40% off.
The Regenstein Macaque Forest outdoor viewing is best before 11am — after that the monkeys nap in the shade.

parentStory.title: The day the polar bear swam with us
parentStory.excerpt: We brought our twin 3-year-olds to the zoo on a perfect 72-degree day. The polar bear exhibit has an underwater viewing window at toddler height. Both boys got down on their knees and the polar bear swam figure-eights above them for ten solid minutes.
parentStory.author: Jenna, mom of twins from Evanston
parentStory.fullStory: It was one of those golden parenting days. Nothing went wrong. The polar bear, Anana, was clearly in a playful mood. She swam laps in the underwater viewing area while my twins sat transfixed. A zoo volunteer came over and explained that Anana was doing her happy dance — a swimming pattern she only does when she is feeling good. We stayed for almost an hour. I took 47 photos. Two of them are framed in our living room.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: McCormick Bird House, Kovler Lion House, polar bear exhibit, Farm-in-the-Zoo petting — 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full loop of all exhibits, plus the Nature Boardwalk, children playground, and a picnic lunch in the park — 4-5 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: All ages, budget-conscious families, repeat visits

name: Smithsonian National Zoo
description: A world-class zoo with free admission as part of the Smithsonian Institution. Famous for its giant pandas (the zoo's panda program has been active since 1972). Home to 2,700 animals across 390 species. The Kids' Farm offers hands-on animal encounters, and the zoo elevated boardwalks give spectacular views of big cats and great apes.
tipsAndTricks: The giant pandas are most active between 8-9:30am during their feeding — arrive by 8am and go straight to the Asia Trail.
Park in the zoo lot ($25 all day, cashless) or take Metro to Woodley Park-Zoo station — street parking is a myth.
The Amazonia exhibit has free-flying birds and a 30-foot indoor waterfall — toddlers find it mesmerizing but hold on to hats.
Bring water and snacks — the zoo allows outside food and on-site options are expensive and have long weekend lines.
The Kids' Farm is closed in winter (November-March). Check the website before going with little ones.

parentStory.title: Panda panda panda
parentStory.excerpt: My daughter's obsession with pandas is well-documented in our house — panda pajamas, panda backpack, panda everything. When we walked into the Panda House and saw Tian Tian eating bamboo three feet away, her face went through five emotions in two seconds. She didn't speak for a full minute. Then she whispered he is real.
parentStory.author: David, dad of 1 from Philadelphia
parentStory.fullStory: We took the train down specifically for this. She turned 6 and all she wanted was to see real pandas. We got there before gates opened. The panda house viewing area has a two-minute max during busy times, but since we were first in the keeper let us stay for almost ten. Our daughter asked the keeper about panda poop. She learned more about giant panda digestion than any human should know. Best birthday ever.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Panda House, Great Ape House, Amazonia, Kids Farm — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All animal exhibits plus the reptile house, Think Tank, and Elephant Trails — 5-6 hours

name: National Air and Space Museum
description: The most visited museum in the United States, housing the world's largest collection of aviation and space artifacts. See the Wright Flyer, Apollo 11 command module, and Space Shuttle Discovery. The interactive exhibits — especially the flight simulators and the How Things Fly physics lab — keep kids engaged for hours. Free admission as part of the Smithsonian.
bestTime: Weekdays 10am-2pm, avoid weekends and school holidays
tipsAndTricks: Timed-entry passes are REQUIRED even though admission is free — book them on recreation.gov at least 2 weeks in advance for weekends.
The flight simulators ($9 per person) have a 38-inch height minimum — measure your kid before they queue for 45 minutes.
The 'How Things Fly' gallery is a hands-on paradise for school-age kids: wind tunnels, paper airplane launchers, and Bernoulli blowers.
Enter through the Mall entrance (Independence Ave) — the other entrance has a longer security line.
The museum is undergoing renovations through 2026 — check which galleries are open before visiting.

parentStory.title: When a 7-year-old corrected the docent
parentStory.excerpt: My son memorized the entire Apollo 11 mission timeline from YouTube videos. At the museum, a docent said Apollo 11's computers had the power of a modern calculator. My son loudly announced it was less — 2.048 MHz with 36K of RAM. The docent paused, grinned, and said he was correct.
parentStory.author: Priya, mom of 2 from Boston
parentStory.fullStory: I was mortified at first — my kid correcting a professional in front of 20 people. But the docent was amazing. She made him her junior expert for the rest of the tour. He got to help explain the lunar module docking mechanism. Other parents were asking me how to get their kids that into space. Three years of Space Train YouTube videos on repeat. It pays off eventually.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Milestones of Flight, Boeing Milestones Hall, flight simulators — 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All main galleries, IMAX film, How Things Fly lab, food court lunch — 4-5 hours

name: New England Aquarium
description: An iconic Boston waterfront aquarium best known for its massive four-story Giant Ocean Tank housing a Caribbean coral reef with sea turtles, stingrays, and sharks. The penguin colony features daily feedings. Touch tanks, the shark and ray touch pool, and a giant-screen theater keep families engaged for hours. Located on the historic waterfront near great dining.
tipsAndTricks: The penguin feeding at 9:15am (right when doors open) is the best show of the day — penguins are energetic and crowds are thin.
Buy the Go Boston card if visiting multiple attractions — you get 20% off aquarium admission bundled with other kid-friendly spots.
The Trust Family Foundation Shark and Ray Touch Pool gets packed — go during the 11am sea lion show when crowds thin out.
Strollers aren't allowed on the upper ramp of the Giant Ocean Tank — babywear or use the elevator between levels.
The aquarium has a Rainy Day policy: if you leave within 30 minutes due to a meltdown, they'll give you a return pass.

parentStory.title: Myrtle the turtle outlived my patience
parentStory.excerpt: Myrtle, a 500-pound green sea turtle, has lived at the aquarium since 1970 — that is 50+ years. My 4-year-old stood at the bottom of the Giant Ocean Tank saying hi Myrtle over and over for 35 straight minutes. Myrtle kept circling back. I timed it. The turtle was more patient than I was.
parentStory.author: Tom, dad of 3 from Cambridge
parentStory.fullStory: I have been coming to this aquarium since I was a kid. Myrtle was here then too. Watching my youngest have the same mesmerized reaction I did three decades ago was surreal. She named Myrtle as her best friend. For weeks after, every bath time was swimming with Myrtle. The aquarium volunteer said Myrtle recognizes patterns and swims toward kids who wave consistently. So maybe it was real.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Giant Ocean Tank, penguin colony, touch pool, Trust Family exhibits — 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All exhibits plus the IMAX theater and a harbor walk lunch — 4 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-12, rainy Boston days, sea life enthusiasts

name: Woodland Park Zoo
description: A nationally ranked zoo set in 92 acres of lush Pacific Northwest landscape. Known for its naturalistic, open-concept habitats that make you feel like you are seeing animals in the wild. Highlights include the award-winning African Savanna with giraffes and zebras, the Tropical Rainforest dome, and the Family Farm petting area. Commitment to conservation is world-class.
tipsAndTricks: Seattle drizzle is a plus — animals are more active in light rain than blazing sun, and crowds thin to almost nothing.
The Zoomazium indoor play center is included with admission and saves the day when the weather turns truly miserable.
Bring rain gear even on sunny mornings — the zoo sits in a microclimate zone where afternoon showers appear fast.
The carousel opens at 11am and tickets are $3 — buy the unlimited ride wristband ($8) if your kid wants more than 3 rides.
Park in the lot on Phinney ($7 with zoo validation) — the neighboring Green Lake neighborhood parking is heavily ticketed.

parentStory.title: Wet gorilla, dry laughter
parentStory.excerpt: It was pouring. The gorilla in the Tropical Rainforest exhibit grabbed a handful of leaves, held them over his head like an umbrella, and walked to a drier spot. My kids lost it laughing.
parentStory.author: Lee, mom of 2 from Portland
parentStory.fullStory: We almost skipped the zoo because of the rain. The gorilla — who the keeper later told us is named Leon — has a reputation for being a thinker. He has been observed using tools, solving puzzles, and apparently inventing umbrellas. My 6-year-old was so impressed that he used a trash bag as a gorilla-style umbrella for the rest of the week.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: African Savanna, Tropical Rainforest, Family Farm, Zoomazium — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full zoo loop, carousel ride, Splash Park (summer), lunch at the zoo, kid discovery garden — 4-5 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-12, rainy day backup plans, preschool-age kids

name: Montreal Biodome
description: A unique indoor nature museum that recreates four distinct ecosystems of the Americas: the Tropical Rainforest, Laurentian Maple Forest, Gulf of St. Lawrence, and Sub-Antarctic Islands. Walk through climate-controlled biomes from steamy jungle to icy polar worlds. The penguin exhibit and the free-flying bird aviary in the Tropical Rainforest are absolute highlights for kids.
location: 4777 Pierre-de Coubertin Ave, Montreal, Quebec H1V 1B3
tipsAndTricks: Dress in layers — you go from 85°F Tropical Rainforest humidity to 45°F Sub-Antarctic within 50 feet.
The penguin feeding is at 11:30am daily — get to the Sub-Antarctic zone 15 minutes early for a good viewing spot.
Buy the Espace pour la Vie pass if you are also visiting the Insectarium, Planetarium, or Botanical Garden — it saves 30% on combined admission.
The Tropical Rainforest aviary has no netting — birds fly freely overhead and one might land near your kid.
Wednesday evenings in summer have reduced admission ($15 adults, free for kids) from 5-8pm.

parentStory.title: Penguin parade changed our trip
parentStory.excerpt: The penguin keepers do an enrichment walk in the morning — the penguins waddle through the Sub-Antarctic exhibit while curious visitors follow. Our 3-year-old waddled WITH them. Full-on penguin walk. The keepers laughed so hard one almost dropped her clipboard.
parentStory.author: Sophie, mom of 2 from Toronto
parentStory.fullStory: We were on a long weekend trip and the Biodome was a filler activity between bigger plans. It ended up being the entire highlight. Our 3-year-old refused to leave. She wanted to watch the penguins swim (they zoom underwater incredibly fast). For her birthday the next month, she requested a Biodome cake — green ganache for the rainforest and white icing for the polar zone. The baker was confused. We weren't.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Two biomes (Tropical + Sub-Antarctic), penguin feeding, interpretive center — 2 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All four biomes, plus the adjacent Insectarium and Botanical Garden — 4-5 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-12, rainy/cold days, animal and nature lovers

name: Quito Zoo (Zoológico de Quito)
description: Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Pichincha volcano at 2,900 meters elevation, Quito Zoo is a conservation-focused facility featuring mostly rescued and endemic animals. See Andean condors with enormous wingspans, spectacled bears, ocelots, and a remarkable collection of native Ecuadorian species. The zoo provides jaw-dropping views of the city below.
location: Av. Pedro Vicente Maldonado s/n, Quito 170180, Ecuador
tipsAndTricks: Acclimate to Quito's altitude (2,850m) for at least 24 hours before visiting — the zoo is uphill and kids feel the thin air fast.
Bring coca tea in a thermos — it helps with altitude adjustment and there is no cafe selling it on site.
The Andean condor feeding is at 10:30am — arrive early to watch the keepers interact with these massive birds.
The path from the entrance to the condor enclosure is steep — babywear toddlers rather than pushing a stroller.
Take a taxi rather than the bus — public transport stops a 20-minute steep walk downhill from the entrance.

parentStory.title: Condor, literally eye-to-eye
parentStory.excerpt: The Andean condor enclosure sits at the edge of a cliff. Our 5-year-old was standing at the safety rail when a condor landed on a rock three feet away and turned its head to look directly at her. The wingspan. Up close.
parentStory.author: Marco, dad of 1 from Cuenca
parentStory.fullStory: I grew up hearing about condors but seeing one at arms length is something else entirely. The keeper told us this one — Guayco — was rescued from illegal trafficking as a chick. Watching my daughter lock eyes with a bird that has a 10-foot wingspan was humbling. She drew condors for a month after.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Andean condor, spectacled bear, native birds section — 2 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full zoo loop, guided tour with keeper talks, picnic with city view — 3-4 hours

name: TelefériQo Cable Car Family Day
description: One of the highest aerial lifts in the world, ascending from 2,950m to 4,053m on the side of Pichincha volcano in just 18 minutes. The views over Quito are spectacular and the summit has hiking trails, horse rentals, a small restaurant, and playground areas. A thrilling family adventure.
tipsAndTricks: Go at 8am SHARP — clouds roll in by 11am and you pay for a ride through fog.
Altitude is no joke at 4,000m+ — buy oxygen cans ($5) at the summit shop and make your kids sip water constantly.
The horse ride at the summit is beginner-friendly and led by guides — costs $15 for 20 minutes and kids love it.
Skip choclo con queso at the summit unless your stomach is iron — altitude plus heavy corn equals regret.
Bring sunscreen and sunglasses — UV is 40% stronger at 4,000m and you will burn in 15 minutes.

parentStory.title: Above the clouds with a 6-year-old
parentStory.excerpt: We rode up through dense cloud cover. Just before the top, we broke through into brilliant sunshine with the peaks of the Andes stretching in every direction. My 6-year-old said we were flying.
parentStory.author: Clara, mom of 1 from Buenos Aires
parentStory.fullStory: I was nervous about the height and the thin air. My son was absolutely fearless. At the top, we hiked a short trail, rented a horse, and ate lunch with a view that stretched across three volcanic peaks. A local guide pointed out Cotopaxi in the distance. My son still talks about the day we went higher than the clouds.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Cable car round trip, summit walk, playground, lunch with view — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Cable car, hiking trail, horse riding, zip line (when available), full restaurant meal — 4-5 hours

name: Parque de las Leyendas Zoo
description: Lima's most famous zoo and botanical garden, set on 37 acres. Divided into three ecological zones: Costa (Coast), Sierra (Highlands), and Selva (Jungle), each housing native animals from those regions. Features a small aquarium, a train ride, and a children farm. More than 1,000 animals including Andean condors, jaguars, and Peruvian hairless dogs.
location: Av. Las Leyendas 580, San Miguel 15087, Lima, Peru
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays — weekends are packed with local families and the train line hits 40-minute waits.
The Selva zone is the most impressive — a walk-through jungle enclosure with monkeys swinging overhead.
Bring cash — not all food stalls accept cards and the ATM at the entrance often runs out on weekends.
The aquarium section is small but the Amazon fish species (paiche, arapaima) are enormous and fascinate kids.
Go early and start in the Sierra zone — condors are most active in the cooler morning hours.

parentStory.title: The jaguar that yawned on cue
parentStory.excerpt: We were at the big cat enclosure when a massive jaguar stretched, yawned, and showed every single tooth to my 4-year-old. My daughter waved. The jaguar blinked slowly.
parentStory.author: Ana, mom of 2 from Miraflores
parentStory.fullStory: My kids think all zoos are the same, but Parque de las Leyendas won them over. The jaguar encounter was the highlight, but they also loved the Peruvian hairless dog exhibit (which is apparently a national treasure) and the large Amazon fish tank. We spent four hours and could have stayed longer.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Sierra zone (condors, bears), Selva zone (jaguar, monkeys), train ride — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All three zones, aquarium, children farm, train, play area, lunch — 5 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-12, Peruvian nature lovers, budget families

seoKeywords: family things to do Lima Peru

name: Bogota Zoo (Jardin Zoologico de Bogota)
description: Bogota's main zoo, located in the Simon Bolivar Park complex, housing over 130 species with a strong focus on Colombian and South American wildlife. The zoo emphasizes conservation education with well-designed habitats. Highlights include Amazonian giant river otters, spectacled bears, pygmy hippos, and a walk-through butterfly garden. One of the most affordable family outings in the city.
location: Carrera 7 No. 1-60, Bogota, Colombia (within Simon Bolivar Park)
tipsAndTricks: Bogota altitude (2,600m) means kids tire faster — take it slow.
Amazonian otter feeding at 10am — otters are incredibly playful and put on a show.
Butterfly garden opens at 10:30 — humid inside, dress lightly.
Weekends are very busy with local families — go on weekdays.
Simon Bolivar Park adjacent has paddle boats and bike rentals for after the zoo.

parentStory.title: Pygmy hippo surprise
parentStory.excerpt: We had no idea pygmy hippos existed. Our son thought it was a baby hippo. The keeper explained they stay this size. He was fascinated.
parentStory.author: Carlos, dad of 2 from Medellin
parentStory.fullStory: The zoo is modest compared to North American standards but has heart. The giant river otters were incredible — zipping through the water like torpedoes. Our son still talks about the pygmy hippos that never grow up.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Amazonian otter, spectacled bear, butterfly garden — 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All exhibits plus guided tour and Simon Bolivar Park boat ride — 4-5 hours

name: Santiago Zoo (Zoologico Nacional de Chile)
description: Chile's national zoo located on San Cristobal Hill with panoramic views of the Andes. Houses over 1,000 animals across 100+ species with focus on Chilean wildlife. Highlights include Andean condors, Chilean flamingos, pumas, and a walk-through aviary. Accessible via funicular which kids love.
location: Parque Metropolitano, San Cristobal Hill, Santiago, Chile
tipsAndTricks: Take the funicular up — it is part of the experience and kids love the cable car ride.
Andean condors are most active around 11am feeding time.
The zoo is on a steep hill — wear comfortable walking shoes.
Bring water and snacks — limited food options inside.
Combine with a visit to the top of San Cristobal Hill for incredible Santiago views.

parentStory.title: Condors meet the city
parentStory.excerpt: We watched a condor perched on a dead branch, the entire city of Santiago spread out behind it. My daughter said it looked like the bird owned everything it could see.
parentStory.author: Maria, mom of 1 from Valparaiso
parentStory.fullStory: San Cristobal Hill is beautiful and the zoo is a gem. The condor exhibit is perfectly positioned so the birds are backlit by the Andes. We took the funicular up, spent 3 hours at the zoo, then walked to the hilltop statue. A perfect day.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Funicular ride, condor exhibit, Chilean animals section, aviary — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full zoo plus San Cristobal Hill summit, cable car, picnic with Andes view — 5 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 3-12, nature lovers, families wanting city views

name: Iguazu Falls Family Tour
description: One of the most spectacular natural wonders in the world. Over 275 waterfalls spanning 2 miles. The Argentine side is perfect for families with well-maintained walkways, a train that kids love, and boat rides that get you close. The Devil Throat viewpoint is accessible by train and short walk.
location: Iguazu National Park, Puerto Iguazu, Misiones, Argentina
tipsAndTricks: Upper Circuit is easiest for young kids — flat, short, incredible views from above.
Take the train to Devil Throat station — the walk on the elevated walkway is flat and stroller-friendly.
Rain ponchos are essential on the Lower Circuit — mist soaks everything.
The boat ride gets you DRENCHED — bring dry clothes. Kids over 6 love it.
Coati (raccoon-like animals) are everywhere — do not feed them, they bite.

parentStory.title: Devil Throat took her breath away
parentStory.excerpt: We walked the elevated platform to Devil Throat. The roar got louder. When we reached the end — 360 degrees of falling water — my 7-year-old just stood with her mouth open. She couldn't speak.
parentStory.author: Ana Paula, mom of 2 from Sao Paulo
parentStory.fullStory: Iguazu has been on my bucket list since I was a kid. Sharing it with my daughter was overwhelming. The moment she saw Devil Throat, she grabbed my hand so tight. We stood there for 15 minutes, mist in our faces, saying nothing.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Upper Circuit walk, Devil Throat train and platform — 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Upper Circuit, Lower Circuit, Devil Throat, boat ride, train loop, lunch — 6-7 hours

name: Montevideo Zoo (Zoologico de Villa Dolores)
description: Uruguay main zoo located in the beautiful Villa Dolores park. Houses a diverse collection of animals including native South American species and some exotics. Features a small aquarium, reptile house, and a children petting area. The park itself is lovely with gardens, playgrounds, and walking paths.
tipsAndTricks: The zoo is inside Villa Dolores park — make a full day of it with the playground and gardens.
Go on a weekday morning — weekends are crowded and the reptile house gets hot.
The petting area (weekends only) has goats and sheep that kids can feed — bring a few pesos for feed.
Montevideo in summer (Dec-Feb) is HOT — go early and bring hats and water.
The aquarium section is small but has interesting Rio de la Plata species.

parentStory.title: A goat with opinions
parentStory.excerpt: The petting zoo goat was not gentle. He nudged my 3-year-old in the back of the knee, she toppled into a hay bale, and the goat immediately started eating her shoelaces.
parentStory.author: Lucia, mom of 3 from Punta del Este
parentStory.fullStory: The zoo is modest but the park setting is lovely. My kids mostly wanted to run around Villa Dolores which has excellent playgrounds. The zoo became a nice bonus. The goat eating shoelaces became a family legend.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Main animal exhibits, reptile house, Villa Dolores park playground — 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full zoo plus park gardens, playground, picnic lunch — 4 hours
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-10, budget travelers, Uruguay family trips

name: Havana Zoo (Zoologico Nacional de Cuba)
description: Cuba's national zoo located in the outskirts of Havana. A sprawling facility with a mix of exotic and endemic species including Cuban crocodiles (Cuban endemic), lions, zebras, ostriches, and native birds. Conditions are more rustic than North American zoos — an adventurous family outing that shows a different side of Havana.
location: Carretera de Capdevila km 3.5, Boyeros, Havana, Cuba
tipsAndTricks: Temper expectations — this is not a modern zoo. It is rustic and real. That is the appeal.
Bring plenty of water and snacks — on-site food options are limited and unreliable.
The Cuban crocodile exhibit is the highlight — these are a critically endangered endemic species.
Cash only (CUP) — cards are not accepted anywhere.
The zoo is far from central Havana — negotiate a taxi fare in advance and ask them to wait.

parentStory.title: Cuban crocodiles up close
parentStory.excerpt: The Cuban crocodile enclosure was basic but the crocs were enormous and active. One swam right up to the glass and my 5-year-old came face-to-face with a 10-foot predator. She asked if it could eat the cat.
parentStory.author: Jose, dad of 1 from Varadero
parentStory.fullStory: I wanted my daughter to see Cuban crocodiles — they are only found in the Zapata Swamp and this zoo. The conditions are not fancy but the animals seem well-cared for and the keepers clearly love them. The keeper let my daughter help toss food to the crocodiles. She still talks about feeding a crocodile.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Cuban crocodiles, big cats, native birds — 2 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full zoo plus picnic lunch in the grounds — 3-4 hours
